title: Hybrid quant calibration & benchmarking pipeline for FP8/INT8 with long-context and batching
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable calibration + validation pipeline that outputs production-ready quantization profiles for both FP8 variants (e4m3/e5m2) and INT8 modes, and run a systematic throughput/latency benchmark matrix that captures batching interactions and long-context behavior.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Calibration: implement hybrid calibration flow supporting per-channel scale estimation with outlier clipping, percentile-based clipping (0.999 / 0.9999), and optional symmetric/asymmetric quant modes. Support both static (offline) and dynamic (on-the-fly) calibration artifacts.
- Profiles: generate profile bundles for: FP8-e4m3, FP8-e5m2, INT8-per-tensor and INT8-per-channel. Tag each bundle with model commit, tokenizer hash, and calibration dataset snapshot id.
- Accuracy validation: run evaluation suite (LM perplexity on heldout tokens, Rouge-L/EM for generation tasks, classification accuracy for discriminative heads) and compute delta vs FP16 baseline. Define regression triggers: >0.8% abs drop for metric-sensitive workloads OR >2.0 perplexity increase on LM tasks.
- Performance benchmarking: automated harness to measure throughput (tokens/sec) and latency P50/P95/P99 across: batch_sizes = [1,4,8,16]; seq_lens = [512,2048,8192]; cache_states = [cold, warm]; kv_cache_enabled = [true,false]; measure both streaming and non-streaming scenarios. Capture memory and GPU utilization.
- Stability & CI: integrate into nightly pipeline. Fail CI if regression triggers fire for a profile marked as "production". Persist artifacts in S3 under s3://redwood-quant/profiles/<model>/<profile-id>.

Design considerations / trade-offs encountered:
- Per-channel INT8 gives better accuracy but larger profile size and slightly higher quant/dequant cost; for certain MLP layers we plan to prefer per-tensor INT8 unless accuracy loss is >0.5%.
- FP8 offers lower memory and faster matmul on some kernels but observed numerical edge cases on normalization layers; the calibration step will include layer-wise outlier diagnostics and an automatic fallback table to INT8 for problematic layers.
- Batching interacts non-linearly with KV cache: warm-cache batched throughput shows diminishing returns at high seq_len; benchmark suite will run both isolated (single-request) and aggregated (many concurrent requests) experiments.

Deliverables:
- calibration/ directory with scripts to generate labelled profile bundles (s3 upload support).
- perf harness to generate a benchmark matrix CSV + Grafana dashboard links.
- acceptance test that compares accuracy against FP16 baseline and flags regressions.
- PR with code changes and accompanying design doc describing clipping/percentile choices.

Notes about datasets and reproducibility:
- Calibration datasets: mix of Reddit-comment style conversational windows (for chat behaviors) and long-form web text for long-context activation patterns. Each run seeds RNGs and stores a manifest.
- Reproducibility: every profile includes the seed, library version, and deterministic torch/cuda flags used during calibration.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype calibration tool + generate profiles for one internal model (r-instruct-1b).
2) Run full benchmark matrix for that model and iterate on clipping heuristics.
3) Promote best-performing profile to dedicated canary on runtime-1.20 for 48h with traffic diverted from non-critical tenants.
4) If stable, publish profile bundles and enable automated selection in the serving runtime with an opt-in flag.
